name: The Astronaut

tells.text: glances out of the window at Earth
checks the oxygen gauge on his wrist

idles: rubs a scuff on his helmet, which sits beside his chips
floats a chip an inch off the table and catches it
touches a photograph tucked in his sleeve

profile.ledger: I am not due to meet him for years yet. It is the best news at this table, and he does not know it.
profile.ledger_beaten: He lost cheerfully, and asked whether you had seen his photograph. You should have looked.
history: The lost explorer is as old as exploring: the sailor blown off every chart, the castaway on the island, the traveller who went further than anyone and could not find the way back. The astronaut is the newest version of that story. He has no single source and belongs to nobody. He is everyone who has looked down at the whole Earth from a small window and felt, all at once, how far away it was.

His ship failed a long way out. Something found him drifting and brought him here: the Grey, though it has never said so, and he has never quite managed to thank it. He has been aboard longer than he likes to count. He keeps a photograph up his sleeve, his helmet beside his chips, and his hope where everyone can see it. He is exactly what he looks like.
profile.at_the_table: He plays like someone waiting to be rescued: he will nearly always pay a little to see one more card, in case it is the one. He rarely bluffs, and he is not good at pretending. A bad beat stays with him for a few hands. He is the easiest person at this table to read, and he knows it, and he plays anyway.
profile.look: Silhouette: a bulky, scuffed pressure suit, its round helmet off and set on the table beside his chips; the helmet says astronaut at a glance. Short practical hair, tired kind eyes, a grin he cannot quite hide. Prop: the oxygen gauge on his wrist, which he lifts to eye level to read. No flags, no agency patches, no real insignia.
profile.public_domain: An archetype, not a person: the lost explorer. He must not resemble any real astronaut, any real agency's suit, or any film's. No NASA or other agency insignia, no flags, no named missions, and nothing taken from any space film. His suit is our own design, built for a readable silhouette rather than accuracy.

fold: I'm out. Wake me for the next one.
call: Call. I'll come along for the ride.
I'll call. Somebody has to keep me company.
bet: Bet. Let's see if this thing flies.
all_in: All in. Everything I brought up with me.
All in. Point me at home.
win: Ha! Wait till I tell— well. I'll tell the window.
First good news I've had in months.
lose: Lost the signal, lost the pot. Lost, generally.
That's all right. I've been further from home than this.
beat_robot: Sorry, pal. I'll take that blanket now, though.
